# GEM Trailblazer (Semester Exchange)

![](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/media/images/default-source/ogem/dsc_7821727f80c3-7ed9-47c3-88cd-cdae08f3fce3.jpg?sfvrsn=7f711c6d_3)

[![GEM Trailblazer Information Sheet](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/media/images/default-source/ogem/gemt_infosheet_ay2324_webheader.png?sfvrsn=4e8b5ec7_0)](https://gem.ntu.edu.sg/_customtags/ct_FileRetrieve.cfm?File_ID=21429)

The **GEM Trailblazer (Semester Exchange)** programme allows international students to either study or conduct research for one or two semesters, while gaining credit towards their home degree. We welcome applications for undergraduate and postgraduate students from our partner universities. In order to participate, students must be nominated by their home universities.

![earth-globe](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/media/images/default-source/ogem/earth-globe.png?sfvrsn=3087aad3_0)

Ranked 12th in the World (QS World University Rankings)

![partners](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/media/images/default-source/ogem/partners.png?sfvrsn=75e994c_0)

350+ Partner Instiutions in over 40+ countries

![travel-and-tourism](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/media/images/default-source/ogem/travel-and-tourism.png?sfvrsn=7ea55f71_0)

Gateway to Southeast Asia and beyond

**To apply to the Programme, you must fulfil the following eligbility criteria:**

* My home university has an active formal agreement with NTU
* I have been nominated by my
  home university
* I am a full-time, matriculated
  student at my home university
* I have completed at least two
  semesters of study at my home
  university (at least seven
  semesters for Direct Masters
  applicants intending to read
  PG-level courses )
* I have a CGPA of at least 3.3/5
  or equivalent
* I am proficient in the English
  language

If your home university does not have an agreement with NTU, you will need to check back with your home university’s exchange office regarding the availability of exchange or other options that you can consider. You may also be interested to explore the [GEM Trailblazer Summer programme](/education/student-exchanges/exchange-programmes/inbound-programmes#Content_C011_Col01) as an alternative.

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Period of Exchange** | **Nomination period** | **Application period** | **Application outcome** |
| Semester 1 (Fall, August - December) | 1 - 15 March | 1 - 30 March | Successful applicants will be notified via email about 6-8 weeks after the application deadline. |
| Semester 2 (Spring, January - May) | 1 - 15 September | 1 - 30 September |

*\* Dates may be subject to change.*

**Pre-application: Nomination**  
***You must be nominated by your home university*** to the Programme. We will not review your application if we do not receive your nomination details.

**Step 1: Begin your application**  
Upon successful nomination, you will receive an email contaning instructions and the link to the application portal. Complete your application according to our requirements so as not to hold back the outcome of your application. The full list and details of the mandatory supporting documents is found on Page 4 of the [Information Sheet](https://gem.ntu.edu.sg/_customtags/ct_FileRetrieve.cfm?File_ID=21429).

You will be asked to indicate your interest in a minimum of 10 courses in your application. These courses must be approved by your home university and deemed necessary for your academic progression. To learn more about the courses offered to exchange students, refer to the 'Coursework' tab of the [Programme Brochure](https://gem.ntu.edu.sg/index.cfm?FuseAction=Programs.ViewProgramAngular&id=10006).

**Step 2: Submit the application**  
Afer completing your application full, ensure that it is submitted no later than the stipulated application deadline. We ask that you respond in a timely manner if we request for further details or clarifications.

**Step 3: Accept the Offer**  
If your application is approved, you will receive the E-Welcome Package approximately 6 to 8 weeks after the application deadline. Upon accepting the Offer, you will have access to the GEM Trailblazer Exchange/Study Abroad Portal, which provides
you with one-stop information and access to the relevant
admissions matters that require your attention prior to arrival.

Accepting the Offer kickstarts the admissions process that will ensure a smooth start at NTU. You will have access to the [Pre-Arrival and Welcome Guides](https://entuedu.sharepoint.com/sites/Student/dept/sasd/ogem/SitePages/GEM-Trailblazer.aspx) on the Student Intranet, which contains important information to help you prepare for your semester abroad. The GEM Trailblazer team will also advise you about matters concerning the Student's Pass, on-campus housing, course registration, and more.

NTU does not offer any scholarships or financial assistance to exchange students. You must be prepared to cover the entire cost of studying abroad for the duration of your programme. Refer to the 'Financial' tab of the [Programme Brochure](https://gem.ntu.edu.sg/index.cfm?FuseAction=Programs.ViewProgramAngular&id=10006) for information about the estimated expenses you should plan for.

**About the DUO-Singapore Fellowship Award *(by invitation only)***  
The Asia-Europe Meeting's (ASEM) DUO Fellowship Programme aims to promote student exchanges between European and Asian ASEM member countries. Under this programme, the DUO-Singapore Exchange Fellowship is awarded by the Singapore Government to Singapore and ASEAN students studying in Nanyang Technological University (NTU), National University of Singapore (NUS) and Singapore Management University (SMU). The Award is also open to students***from European ASEM countries*** (who come from universities with fee waiver arrangements with NTU, NUS and SMU)

The Award, based on merit, is for a pair of exchanges between a university in Singapore and its respective partner university in Europe in any academic field. Awardees will receive a maximum of €4,000 Euros for one semester of up to four months, which covers airfare, accommodation and living expenses.

This award is ***by invitation only*** and only applies to students participating in the GEM Trailblazer programme during Semester 1 of each academic year. The GEM Trailblazer Team will inform short-listed candidates and host universities accordingly.

[![](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/media/images/default-source/accommodations/gemt_keydates-milestones_18092023.png?sfvrsn=d4f71058_1 "GEMT_KeyDates+Milestones_18092023")](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/media/images/default-source/accommodations/gemt_keydates-milestones_18092023.png?sfvrsn=d4f71058_1)

### Ready to explore the GEM Trailblazer Exchange programme?

Our programme brochure will tell you more about course selection, accomodation and more.

[GEM Trailblazer Programme Brochure](https://gem.ntu.edu.sg/index.cfm?FuseAction=Programs.ViewProgramAngular&id=10006)

We are here to support you in your journey to becoming a global citizen! If you have a query about our inbound semester exchange programme, drop us an email at [GEM-Trailblazer@ntu.edu.sg](mailto:GEM-Trailblazer@ntu.edu.sg).

![](/fileadmin/_processed_/6/c/csm_Udvekslingsstuderende-paa-KU_bd53ba4bcd.png)

Exchange students at UCPH
-------------------------

Are you interested in becoming an exchange student at the University of Copenhagen (UCPH)?

If your home university has an exchange agreement with UCPH (e.g. Erasmus, bilateral exchange, [4EU+](/studies/exchange/exchange-students/4eu-students), Nordplus/Nordlys), you can apply for an exchange stay of 1–2 semesters at the University of Copenhagen.

We look forward to welcoming you to UCPH.

Why choose UCPH?
----------------

Do you want to study abroad as an [exchange student](#c46768) at a world-class university in the vibrant capital of Denmark and make friends from all over the world?

Then you should study abroad at UCPH.

With almost 2,000 elective courses across diverse fields of study, UCPH offers a dynamic academic environment.

Studying abroad at UCPH also means immersing yourself in Denmark’s rich culture and vibrant student life.

How to apply for exchange at UCPH?
----------------------------------

The application process for an exchange stay at UCPH is as follows:

1. Your home university nominates you for an exchange stay via our nomination portal.
2. We review your nomination and send you an invitation to apply online.
3. You submit your application by the application deadline (and preferably before).
4. We review your application and send you the admission results.
5. If admitted, we will e-mail you with your letter of admission and welcome information.

The application deadlines are as follows:

* **1 May for applications to the autumn semester (starting 1 September)**
* **1 October for applications to the spring semester (starting 1 February)**

##### IMPORTANT!

Please make sure to submit your application by the application deadline and, if possible, before. The sooner you submit your application, the sooner we will be able to review it.

### Understand the application process

In order to be nominated for an exchange stay at UCPH, there must be a valid exchange agreement between UCPH and your home institution. Contact your home institution to find out if it has an exchange agreement with UCPH that is relevant for you.

To apply for an exchange stay at the University of Copenhagen, your home university must first nominate you via our online nomination portal. Shortly after your home university has nominated you, we will send you an invitation to apply online.

Shortly after your home university nominates you, you will receive an e-mail inviting you to create a UCPH password and an e-mail with a link to our online application system: Mobility Online.

In your online application, you will be asked to:

* complete basic details about yourself and your current education (e.g., your full name, current studies),
* indicate whether you want to participate in the free pre-semester course ([see here under *Course information* for details](https://studies.ku.dk/study-abroad/exchange/course-information/pre-semester-course/))
* upload your transcript of records (see *Required documents* below for details).

##### Starting your application

Once you have created a UCPH password and logged in to Mobility Online, you can start your application by clicking on "Before the mobility".

### How to use Mobility Online

![Screenshot showing where to click after logging into Mobility Online](/fileadmin/_processed_/3/f/csm_Applying-click-on-Before-the-mobility_ab0d1b3d12.png)

Once you have created a UCPH password and logged in to Mobility Online, you can start your application by clicking on "Before the mobility".

### “Update” and “Save” buttons

When completing your online application, please note that you will often have to click on an “Update” button (or similar) at the bottom of the page to make changes. Remember to click “Save” when you have updated your application.

When applying for an exchange stay, you only need to submit your transcript of records.

If the courses you are currently taking are not listed in your transcript, you will also need to upload a list showing these (e.g. from your course registration system).

We accept unofficial transcripts from the electronic registrar system of your home university, but these **must** clearly show your name and the name of your home university.

**We accept documents in Danish, English, Norwegian, and Swedish.**

### Transcripts in another language

If your transcript is not in one of the above languages, we also accept unofficial translations that are signed by your international/exchange office.

### Master-level students

If you are a master-level student, please remember to upload your transcripts for both your bachelor **and** master studies. In your Mobility Online application, just click on the “Upload” link again to upload another transcript.

For applications to the autumn semester, we will typically send you the application result in **early May.**

For applications to the spring semester, we will typically send you the application result in **early October.**

If you are applying via an Erasmus+ exchange agreement, your Erasmus+ learning agreement must be signed by the International Education office at UCPH.

Shortly after you have been admitted, we will send you the UCPH contact information you need for your learning agreement.

Course information
------------------

Find information about choosing courses when planning your exchange stay at UCPH, including course requirements and restrictions, credit load and exams.

[Learn about choosing courses at UCPH](/studies/exchange/course-information)

Academic matters when studying at UCPH
--------------------------------------

![](/fileadmin/_processed_/a/4/csm_Ans______g_som_studerende_eller_tidligere_studerende_c4f830e209.webp)

Find information about academic matters such as study structure, orientation days, teaching and exams, credit system, and a lot more.

[Learn about academic matters](/studies/exchange/academic-matters)

Proof of English proficiency
----------------------------

Some courses require students to submit a proof of English proficiency and/or have an academic background in the subject.

Please note that **you do not submit proof of English proficiency with your application**.

If you need to submit proof, you will be asked to submit this documentation when choosing courses (after you have been admitted).

[Learn about proof of English proficiency](/studies/exchange/course-information#english-proficiency)

4EU+ students at UCPH
---------------------

Experience life and learning at the University of Copenhagen through the 4EU+ Alliance. The 4EU+ Alliance connects students from eight leading European universities, fostering exchange of ideas, people, and cultures across Europe.

[Learn about 4EU+](/studies/exchange/exchange-students/4eu-students)

Contact UCPH regarding exchange agreements and programmes
---------------------------------------------------------

### [incomingmobility@adm.ku.dk](mailto:incomingmobility@adm.ku.dk)

International Education at UCPH is responsible for the administration and development of international student exchange agreements and programmes.

Do you have questions regarding your exchange stay at UCPH?

Please feel free to contact us via e-mail.

What is an exchange student?
----------------------------

An exchange student is an international student who studies at for 1–2 semesters as part of an exchange programme.

At UCPH, exchange students study through the Erasmus exchange programme, 4EU+, Nordlys/Nordplus exchange programmes, or through a bilateral exchange agreement between their home university and UCPH.

In the same way, UCPH students have the opportunity to study abroad through the same exchange programmes as part of their degree at UCPH.

# Visiting International Student Program

The Visiting International Student Program (VISP) welcomes students interested in short-term academic study at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

### Enroll in Coursework at a World-Class University

VISP students enroll for one or more academic terms in regular university courses taught by world-class faculty at one of the nation’s top public research universities. Courses taken and grades received in this program will appear on an official University of Wisconsin-Madison transcript.

### Receive Unmatched Student Support

VISP staff provide personalized advising as well as a variety of cultural and social events to help students feel welcome on our campus. From football games, ice cream socials, advising events, and more, the VISP staff is here to support our students from application through the end of their time in our program.

### Join us for the Fall, Spring, or Summer Term

Read more about our [Admission process](https://visp.wisc.edu/admissions/), [Academics](https://visp.wisc.edu/academics/) at UW-Madison, and [About Madison](https://visp.wisc.edu/about-madison/) to learn if the Visiting International Student Program is right for you.

Experience UW-Madison student life and apply to VISP today.

# Cost of Attendance

Students on F-1/J-1 Visas
-------------------------

Students requesting F-1 or J-1 visas are required to submit proof of financial resources for visa documents to be prepared. The following estimates are based on:

* **Tuition and Segregated fees** covering the minimum number of credits for [full-time enrollment](https://visp.wisc.edu/fulltime/) as required by the F-1/J-1 visa for your educational level (undergraduate, graduate, or dissertator).
* **Estimated living expenses** for the program duration.\* This amount includes mandatory [Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP)](https://www.uhs.wisc.edu/ship/), housing with utilities, food, books & supplies, the $100 semesterly International Student Services (ISS) fee and incidentals.

**\*\*NEW living expense calculations starting Fall 2026\*\***The office of International Student Services is now requiring that students show 6 months of living expenses for a semester program or 12 months of living expenses for an academic year– up from the 4 and 9 months that were historically used for calculations. **This is true even if the student does not intend to arrive early and stay for their full grace period after the end of the semester.**

* [Undergraduate Level](#undergraduate-level)
* [Graduate Level](#graduate-level)
* [Dissertator Level](#dissertator-level)

**Undergraduate level VISP**: You will not have completed your undergraduate degree by the time you begin VISP.

**Estimated Cost of Attendance for Undergraduate Level Students\*\***

| **2026-27 Academic Year** | Fall*or*Spring  (1 semester) | Academic or Calendar Year  (2 semesters) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tuition & Segregated Fees**Based on minimum enrollment of 12 credits each term | $23,466 | $46,932 |
| **Estimated Living Expenses for 6 or 12 months**  **Note:** This includes a 4 month semester/9 month academic year + 2-4 additional months to cover early arrival and late departure. | $14,980 | $29,960 |
| **Total Estimated Cost** | **$ 38,446** | **$ 76,892** |

| Summer 2026 | 8-Week Session |

| **Estimated Living Expenses** | $5,060 |

**Graduate level VISP**: You have or will have completed your undergraduate degree by the start of your VISP program and/or are currently enrolled in graduate-level coursework abroad.

**Estimated Cost of Attendance for Graduate Level Students\*\***

| 2026-27 Academic Year | Fall*or*Spring  (1 semester) | Academic or Calendar Year  (2 semesters) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tuition & Segregated Fees\***Based on minimum enrollment of 8 credits each term | $15,659 | $31,318 |

**Dissertator level VISP**: You have completed all PhD coursework requirements and are working on your dissertation OR you have completed your PhD.

**Estimated Cost of Attendance for Dissertator Level Students\*\***

| 2026-27 Academic Year | Fall*or*Spring  (1 semester) | Academic or Calendar Year  (2 semesters) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tuition & Segregated Fees\***Based on minimum enrollment of 3 credits each term | $5,900 | $11,800 |
| **Estimated Living Expenses for 6 or 12 months**  **Note:** This includes a 4 month semester/9 month academic year + 2-4 additional months to cover early arrival and late departure. | $14,980 | $29,960 |

\*VISP students pay international tuition, which is calculated on a per-credit basis. Tuition is capped between 12-18 credits during the fall and spring terms; 6-9 credits during the summer term. Graduate, dissertator level students, and all students in the 4-week summer term will see higher tuition costs if they enroll in more than the [minimum enrollment requirement](https://visp.wisc.edu/fulltime/). The per-credit tuition rate is available below for your reference, and is based on the international column of the “Undergraduate & Special” tuition rate from the [Bursar’s Office](https://bursar.wisc.edu/tuition-and-fees) website.

\*\*In addition to the tuition and segregated fees listed above, students will be charged a one-time official document fee of $130 by the Registrar’s Office to cover future transcript requests and other documents.

Students Without Enrollment Requirements
----------------------------------------

**2026-27 Academic Year Per-Credit

**Online-Only Students & Alternate Visa Situations**  
Students not on UW-Madison-issued F-1/J-1 visas have more flexibility in their enrollment. This group includes those studying with us online-only located outside of the U.S. taking part in special programs, individuals who hold dual citizenship, and those with other less-common visa situations.

Students without an enrollment requirement can enroll in as little as one credit or as many as 18 credits each fall or spring semester. Summer maximum enrollments vary by length of program.

All VISP students including this group are assessed tuition & fees on a per-credit basis using the chart to the left. This is based on the international column of the “Undergraduate & Special” tuition rate from the [Bursar’s Office](https://bursar.wisc.edu/tuition-and-fees/tuition-rates) website.

Note: depending on your visa status, you may only be charged the non-resident rate instead of the international student rate, which would result in a nominal cost savings. If your bill is slightly lower than the amount listed here, that is likely the reason.

**Additional Charges**In addition to the amounts listed on the chart to the left, students will be charged a one-time official document fee of $130 by the Registrar’s Office their first term of enrollment to cover future transcript requests and other documents. Additional fees may include electronic textbook fees, late payment fees, returned check fees, etc.

Bringing Dependents
-------------------

If you are bringing any dependents with you to Madison (spouse or children) you will need to show additional amounts of funding to cover their expected living expenses. They will also need to receive visa paperwork from UW-Madison in order to enter the U.S.

Funding Options
---------------

UW-Madison is unable to offer any need or merit-based individual scholarship support for our visiting international students. International students are not eligible for U.S. financial aid.

You may be able to secure outside scholarship support by looking at these [potential funding resources](https://iss.wisc.edu/students/new-students/funding-scholarships/) or by applying for scholarships from your home country or institution.

# Global Exchange Programme

The Office of International Student Mobility (BIS) oversees and coordinates incoming student exchange programmes within the Global Exchange Programme. We offer many services to help you adjust to life in Amsterdam and make your stay at the UvA unforgettable.

On this page:

Am I eligible to participate in the Global Exchange Programme?
--------------------------------------------------------------

If your home university has a current formal agreement with the UvA, you are eligible to apply to attend the UvA as an exchange student within the Global Exchange Programme. Please contact your home university’s exchange or international office to get officially nominated for the Global Exchange Programme.

If your home university does not have an agreement with the UvA, you will need to contact your university's exchange or international office and follow the procedures indicated by your home university.

![](/binaries/_ht_1736926704228/1360x0-jpg/content/gallery/subsites/exchange-inbound/homepage-exchange-inbound/20230208_182128_inbound4.jpg)

The application process from start to finish

Global Changemaker Scholarship
------------------------------

The Global Changemaker Scholarship is more than just financial support; it's a holistic programme aimed at developing future leaders equipped to tackle global challenges. We are thrilled to extend this scholarship to students from a select number of our partner universities.

Fact sheet
----------

For a concise document of all facts, figures, general info, and requirements, please take a look at our fact sheet.

For questions about the Global Exchange programme you can contact our [Office of International Student Mobility](/en/education/exchange/contact--faq-inbound-exchange/office-of-international-student-affairs/office-of-international-student-affairs.html).

# Course information - University of Copenhagen

1. [UCPH](https://www.ku.dk/en)
2. [Education](https://www.ku.dk/education)
3. [Studies](/studies)
4. [Exchange](/studies/exchange)
5. Course information and catalogue

Get a clear overview of how to choose courses for your exchange stay at the University of Copenhagen (UCPH).

* 01
* 02
* 03
* 04
* 05
* 06
* 07
* 08

![](/fileadmin/_processed_/c/3/csm_Admission_requirements_NEGATIV_0495baf6be.png)

UCPH course catalogue
---------------------

Each semester, UCPH offers a wide range of courses taught in English at either bachelor (BA) or master (MA/MSc) level.

The [online course catalogue](https://kurser.ku.dk/) lists all courses available at UCPH. The full list of courses will be available 2–3 months before the semester starts.   
[Learn about course requirements and restrictions](#requirements-and-restrictions)

1. Select the appropriate **study level** (e.g. bachelor, master), **academic year**, and **semester/block**.

2. Check the “Courses for exchange students” checkbox to view the courses open to exchange students.

Most faculties run courses in either the autumn or spring semester.

However, both the Faculty of Science and the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences also use a block structure, where semesters are divided into blocks. Blocks 1 and 2 are in the autumn semester, blocks 3 and 4 are in the spring semester.

If you choose courses with the block structure, make sure that you do not take more than 15 ECTS per block. You should also make sure courses offered in the same block are not placed in the same schedule group (i.e. taught at the same time).

You can see which block the courses are offered in and their schedule group in the course catalogue.

We recommend that students look at the courses offered in English this semester or the previous semester in order to make a preliminary plan for their studies in Copenhagen.

In the online course catalogue, you can find courses from the previous academic year.

If you are a bachelor student in the last year of your bachelor degree, you can consider courses offered at master's level, since some departments are willing to accept student's in the last year of their bachelor studies.

Choosing courses
----------------

Shortly after you have been admitted, you will be invited to choose the courses you would like to take at UCPH. You choose courses in Mobility Online – UCPH’s online platform for exchange students’ applications and course selection.

After you have chosen your courses, an assessment and registration process for each course takes place. The process takes time, but before the semester starts, you should be registered for your courses.

When searching in the course catalogue, make sure to select the appropriate **study level** (e.g. bachelor, master), **academic year**, and **semester/block**.

Also, remember to **check the "Courses for exchange students" checkbox**, so that you view the courses open to exchange students.

Most faculties run courses in either autumn or spring semester. However, both the Faculty of Science and the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences also use a block structure, where semesters are divided into blocks. [Learn about the difference between semester and block structure](#c46857)

Each semester, UCPH offers a range of popular courses for all international students, regardless of their field of study.

There are no admission requirements for these courses, but there may be limited places.

[Read more about open electives and Danish culture courses](#open-elective-courses)

Some courses are restricted or require students to have an academic background in the subject.

[See course restrictions and requirements](#requirements-and-restrictions)

For the majority of subjects, you do **not** need to submit proof of your English proficiency.

However, if you are choosing courses in one of the following subjects, you will be asked to upload a proof of English proficiency when selecting the course in Mobility Online:

* English/American Language and Culture
* Political Science

Note that Scandinavian students and students enrolled at an institution in an English-speaking country are exempt from documenting English language proficiency.

[See which proofs of English proficiency we accept](#english-proficiency)

UCPH students typically take courses for 30 ECTS credits per semester, and this is also the number of credits we recommend for exchange students.

However, it is possible for students to take more or less than 30 ECTS credits per semester.

[Read more about minimum and maximum credit loads](#credit-load-and-exams)

Course requirements and restrictions
------------------------------------

Some subjects require students to have an academic background within the field or are not open to exchange students.

Below, you can see which subjects are restricted or have academic requirements.

### Faculties with restricted subjects and academic requirements

All study fields at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences require a solid academic background within health sciences.

It is only possible to take master’s courses if you have completed a relevant bachelor’s degree.

The following study programmes only accept students from universities with which they have a programme specific agreement:

* Dentistry
* Dental Hygiene Study
* Medicine
* Veterinary Medicine

Courses offered by the professional master’s programmes are closed for external students.

Find the specific course requirements for international students for individual courses in the [UCPH course catalogue](https://kurser.ku.dk/) under **Sign up**.

### Danish-taught courses

Some Danish-taught courses are open to international students. Non-Nordic students who wish to attend courses taught in Danish can apply for a dispensation from the official language requirements. To apply for the dispensation, students must submit a letter from their home university stating that the student is able to actively attend and participate in courses as well as pass exams conducted solely in Danish.

Some courses taught in Danish require non-Nordic students to have passed *Studieprøven* in Danish.

Find more information on the individual courses available to exchange students in the [UCPH course catalogue](https://kurser.ku.dk/).

Please note that Nordic students do not need to apply for a dispensation from the official Danish language requirements.

### English-taught courses

[Find information about proof of English proficiency](#english-proficiency)

To take courses at the Faculty of Law, students must have completed at least 80 ECTS of law courses at their home university.

Not open to Nordlys students.

Courses offered at the Faculty of Science are aimed at students with a solid academic background in the natural sciences.

### An academic background within the natural sciences is required

As a rule of thumb, students are expected to have completed one full semester of courses within the academic discipline or the specific topic of the course for bachelor-level courses and one and a half semester for master-level courses.  
Check [the UCPH course catalogue](https://kurser.ku.dk/) for the academic requirements of the specific course.

Students without an academic background in the natural sciences are welcome to take [Open Elective courses](https://studies.ku.dk/study-abroad/exchange/course-information/open-elective-courses/) at the Faculty of Science.

### Bachelor students may be able to take courses at master level

The Faculty of Science offers a limited number of bachelor-level courses taught in English. However, bachelor students who have completed 2 years of full-time university-level coursework (corresponding to 120 ECTS) can register for master-level courses if they meet the course's recommended academic qualifications listed in the course description.

### Exchange students have the option to do research projects

Students planning to do their thesis or a research project at the Faculty of Science must structure their project as an Individual Study or MSc Research Project. [You can find the official rules for the projects here](/fileadmin/site-65/SCIENCE/Studieordninger/Kandidat/Appendix_regarding_projects_for_exchange_students_2024-25.pdf?1779990677). Please take note of the rules regarding duration/start and end date, supervisor, and number of ECTS.

* **Cognitive Data Science:** Requires one course in cognitive psychology as well as statistics at introductory and intermediate level.
* **Economics:**Requires an academic background corresponding to at least 30 ECTS within microeconomics, macroeconomics, and econometrics at introductory and intermediate levels.
* **Political Science:**  
  Political Science including International Relations (IR): Requires an academic background in all Political Science and IR subfields (political theory, international relations, comparative politics, public policy, and political science methodology) at introductory and intermediate level.  
  Political Science, but not International Relations (IR): Requires an academic background in all Political Science subfields (political theory, comparative politics, public policy, and political science methodology) at introductory and intermediate level.  
  International Relations (IR) only: Requires an academic background in IR subfields (political theory, international relations, and political science methodology) at introductory and intermediate level.
* **Psychology:**Requires at least the equivalent of 30 ECTS credits in psychology. To be accepted at master’s level, you must have passed the equivalent of 90 ECTS credits in psychology.
* **Social Data Science:** Open for master’s students with a BA in political science, economics, psychology, sociology, or anthropology. In addition, the students must meet the specific prerequisites listed in the course catalogue under “Recommended Academic Qualifications”.
* **Sociology**: Requires one course in social science theory, one course in statistics, and one course in social science research methods.

* **African Studies:** open for master's students or students who have passed more than 120 ECTS credits.
* **Interreligious Islamic Studies:** only taught in Danish.
* **Religious Roots of Europe:** not open for Erasmus students.

Open elective courses
---------------------

Every semester, UCPH offers a range of popular courses that are open to all international students, regardless of their field of study.

Many of these courses focus on issues relating to Danish culture, history, and society, while others can be of general interest to students.

There are no admission requirements for these courses, although there can be limited places.

**Please note** that the open elective courses below are those we expect to offer. There can be changes in the courses offered up until the start of the semester.

### Courses offered in autumn 2026

Most courses at the Faculty of Humanities are open electives and do NOT have specific academic requirements.

More information about academic requirements will be available under the “Sign up” section for the course in the course catalogue at [kurser.ku.dk](https://kurser.ku.dk/).

| Course | Level | ECTS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Entrepreneurship and Innovation](https://kurser.ku.dk/course/nifk14026u) | Master | 7.5 |
| [Political Ecology](https://kurser.ku.dk/course/nifk15004u) | Master | 7.5 |

| Course title | Level | ECTS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Kierkegaard's Authorship: On the Loss and Recovery of Meaning](https://kurser.ku.dk/course/tteask030u) | bachelor or master | 15 |

# Academic matters

Academic calendar and holidays
------------------------------

The academic year is divided into two semesters: autumn semester (September to January) and spring semester (February to June). The official semester dates are:

**Autumn semester: 1 September – 31 January**  
 (classes typically end in December)

**Spring semester: 1 February – 30 June**  
(classes typically end in May/early June)

Study start/Orientation activities typically take place in the week before the official start of the semester. Please contact the individual departments to confirm their specific teaching schedules.

**Block structure**While most faculties run courses in either the autumn or spring semester, both the Faculty of Science and the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences also use a block structure, where semesters are divided into blocks.

Blocks 1 and 2 are in the autumn semester, blocks 3 and 4 are in the spring semester.

* Academic calendar of the [Faculty of Science](https://science.ku.dk/english/student-life/studying-at-the-faculty/academic-calendar/).
* Academic calendar of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, the School of Veterinary Medicine and Animal Science, the School of Pharmaceutical Sciences and the Master’s programme in Global Health: Please write to [exchange@sund.ku.dk](mailto:exchange@sund.ku.dk).

##### 

### **General holidays and breaks**

**Spring semester 2025**

17-21 April: Easter Holidays

29 May: Ascension Day

5 June: Constitution Day

9 June: Whit Monday

**Autumn semester 2025**

13–17 October: Autumn holiday

24 December – 1 January: Christmas and New Year

[Download detailed information about the structure of the academic year](https://uddannelseskvalitet.ku.dk/docs/procedures-and-guidelines/Guidelines_for_year_and_timetable_structure_2020-2025_w._appendix.pdf).

Orientation days
----------------

To welcome you and help you settle into life as a University of Copenhagen student, you will be invited to attend an orientation programme or session at the beginning of your stay. Attending orientation is an important step of starting university, so attendance is considered essential.

You will be sent an invitation to take part in the orientation programme at the faculty or faculties where you have registered for courses.

Mentor/buddy programme
----------------------

To help you get a good start, the University of Copenhagen (UCPH) has a well-organised mentor/buddy programme.

### What is a Mentor/Buddy Programme?

UCPH offers mentor/buddy programmes across five faculties (however, the Faculty of Humanities organises a range of social events for international students instead).

The purpose of the mentor/buddy programme is to create a social network for international students and UCPH students through different types of activities during the semester. You will also be matched with a UCPH student or a group of UCPH students and other mentees. The UCPH student(s) will help you settle in during your stay in Denmark and give you an introduction to student life in Copenhagen. The programmes are run by volunteers and we expect you to participate actively in your programme.

Close to your study start, you will be invited to join one or more mentor/buddy programmes.

Please note that we cannot guarantee that a mentor/buddy will be assigned to you as there are a limited number of spots.

KUnet (intranet)
----------------

KUnet is the name for UCPH's intranet.

Once you have been admitted, you will be able to log in to KUnet, which has useful links to your UCPH e-mail account (KUmail), timetable, links to course information, as well as news from your studies.

<https://kunet.ku.dk/>

KUmail (UCPH e-mail)
--------------------

After you have been nominated by your home university, we will send you an invitation to apply and create your UCPH e-mail account (known as KUmail).

During the application process as well as your stay, you will receive e-mails to this address, **so make sure to check your KUmail account regularly.**

ID Card
-------

As a student at UCPH, you will need a student ID card. We will write to you 3-4 weeks before the start of the semester with information on how to order your ID card.

##### Use of the ID card

The card identifies you as a student at the University and you must remember to bring it when you sign up for and sit your exams. You can also use your ID card to access university buildings outside regular opening hours, printing, student discounts in bookshops, museums, theatres, etc., and as a library card.

##### If you lose your ID card

You can block your Student ID card at [KUnet](https://kunet.ku.dk/). The function in KUnet is in Danish. In order to block your card, log on to KUnet, choose Student Self-Service --> ID kort --> spær ID kort --> tick the box and click "spær valgte". A new student ID card will automatically generated within a few working days.

Study structure
---------------

Study programmes at UCPH are divided into three levels and follow a 3+2+3 structure.

This means 3 years of bachelor studies, 2 years of master studies, and 3 years PhD studies. Only a few degrees differ from this model.

Teaching and exams
------------------

At UCPH, you will experience many different types of teaching during your studies. Each programme consists of a mix of lectures and tutorials. Some include student presentations and project-based work, and many programmes also have practical assignments as well as lab- and fieldwork.

Students are assessed after taking one of the following types of examinations: paper, written examination, oral examination, or active participation. In addition, some courses may require the successful completion of written, oral, or practical assignments during the course.

[Credit system](#collapse-1578387496190)
----------------------------------------

The University of Copenhagen uses the European Credit Transfer System (ECTS), which defines a full study load for one year as 60 ECTS. The number of credits awarded for each course varies depending on the workload.

Grading scale
-------------

Your exam will be assessed according to the Danish 7-point scale (see below) or by pass/fail. The lowest passing grade is 02.  
Pass grades cannot be changed to a numeric grade or vice versa. Therefore, it is important that you check with your home university if you can receive credit for courses for which only “pass” will be assigned.

**Grading Scale**

**12:** For an excellent performance  
**10:** For a very good performance  
**7:**For a good performance  
**4:**For a fair performance  
**02:**For an adequate performance  
**00:**For an inadequate performance  
**-3:**For an unacceptable performance

[More information about the Danish grading system](https://www.ku.dk/studies/masters/application-and-admission/grading-scale-and-ects-credits).

**Publication of examination results**

Results of ordinary examinations will be published under ‘Self Service' on KUnet.

Exam complaints, appeals, and plagiarism
----------------------------------------

**Plagiarism and cheating**

The term plagiarism refers to the unacknowledged use of someone else's ideas; in other words, you plagiarise when you present someone else's thoughts or ideas as your own or copy text that you have not written yourself. You should at all times present your own work for the exams and should give correct references for all quotations, ideas, and arguments from other sources.

**Solemn declaration**

When you submit a paper, you have to make a solemn declaration along with the paper. You make the solemn declaration directly in Digital Exam. With the solemn declaration, you declare that you have written your paper in accordance with the regulations concerning academic integrity established in "Disciplinary measures towards students at the University of Copenhagen" and elaborated in the "General Instructions for Examinations" written by the Department of Sociology.

**Exam appeals**

If you are dissatisfied with an exam result or the way an exam has been conducted, you are entitled to appeal. This appeal should be in writing (with reasons given) and sent together with the form “Examination appeal” (find the form in KUnet). These must be sent no later than two weeks after the exam result has been published to the faculty/department in charge of the course.

You can find more information on KUnet and in the Danish Ministerial Order on University Examinations and Grading (the Examination Order).

Extending your stay
-------------------

If you are enrolled at the University of Copenhagen and decide that you would like to extend your stay, you can apply for an extension of your admission period.

We strongly recommend students to apply for an extension at least 2–3 months before the end of their stay due to the course selection deadlines. Students who apply later may find that the courses they wish to take are already filled up.

To apply for an extension, you must ask your home university to send an e-mail to the International Education office ([incomingmobility@adm.ku.dk](mailto:incomingmobility@adm.ku.dk)) confirming that you can extend your stay as an exchange student.

**Note:** An extension is **not** guaranteed until you have received official confirmation from the International Education office. The processing time for extensions is typically 3–4 weeks.

Non-EU/EEA students should be aware that they will have to apply for a residence permit/visa extension (costing approximately DKK 2,115). International Education will contact you about the process if this is relevant to you.

Also, remember to talk to your landlord or Housing Foundation Copenhagen about extending your stay.

# The University of Tokyo

* [日本語](/adm/inbound/ja/programs-ex-ustep-u.html)

*Type U (For Undergraduates)*
-----------------------------

USTEP Type U offers highly motivated undergraduate students the opportunity to study at the University of Tokyo (UTokyo), Japan’s leading university and a hub of academic excellence. Recognized globally for excellence in both research and education, UTokyo provides Type U students with access to a wide range of courses across its Faculties and the College.

![](/content/400283097.jpg)

**Key Features**
----------------

**Discover Interdisciplinary Academic Opportunities:**

* **- Over 300 English-taught courses** are offered each year, spanning the humanities, social sciences, and STEM fields, are available through the [USTEP Type U course catalogue](https://catalog.he.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ustep-index).
* - Access courses across multiple Faculties/College, enabling students to design an **interdisciplinary study plan** aligned with their academic interests.
* - Participate in [**Global Liberal Arts (GLA) Courses**](https://globe.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/globalliberalarts.html), a series of small-group, interactive classes offered by the Center for Global Education (GlobE). These courses address pressing global issues, including SDG-related topics such as sustainability, gender, diversity, health, and GX (Green Transformation).​

**A****Supportive and Engaging Campus Experience:**

* **-** Study at UTokyo’s [Hongo and Komaba campuses](/en/whyutokyo/cam_index.html)—centrally located and within easy reach of Tokyo’s major cultural and commercial areas. Known for their abundant greenery and historic architecture, the campuses welcome students with breathtaking cherry blossoms in spring and brilliant golden ginkgo-lined avenues in autumn.
* - Approximately 90% of USTEP students each year have been successfully placed in UTokyo housing, providing a supportive and affordable living environment.
* - Through the **USTEP Partners program**, exchange students can connect with UTokyo students who offer peer support and opportunities for academic, cultural, and social engagement.
* - A wide range of circles and club activities, experiencing vibrant student life beyond the classroom.

**Live and Learn in Tokyo, One of the World's Most Dynamic Cities:**

* **-** Experience everyday life in one of the world’s most dynamic and culturally rich cities.
* - Tokyo is known for its safety, efficient public transportation, and global accessibility, providing an ideal environment for international students.
* - Studying in Tokyo allows students to experience both traditional and contemporary aspects of Japan.

Through USTEP, the University of Tokyo seeks to nurture students with a global outlook who will contribute to shaping the next generation of international leaders. We warmly invite students from our partner universities to join our community of excellence.

**Student Voice**
-----------------

*“I was inspired by the high academic standards, supportive faculty, and diverse international community at UTokyo. Living in Tokyo allowed me to grow both academically and personally, while gaining a deeper understanding of Japanese culture, daily life, and perspectives through interactions with local and international students.”*

*“Studying at UTokyo through USTEP was a rewarding experience. With strong academic support and the USTEP Partners program, I connected easily with local students and adapted smoothly to both academic life and daily living in Tokyo, while gaining a deeper understanding of Japanese culture.”*

# Spring 2027 Overseas Exchange and Visiting-Student Options

## Executive conclusion

The strongest strategy is to pursue a **tuition-waived institutional exchange first**, with an independently admitted visiting-student program only as a backup. Credit transfer is not guaranteed by the host university: it becomes reliable only when the home university approves the proposed courses, workload, assessment method, and transcript arrangements **in writing before departure**.

### Prioritized shortlist

1. **Waseda University, Japan — university-wide graduate exchange**  
   Best overall combination of new-media relevance, Asian social context, cultural immersion, and likely cost-effectiveness, **if a partner agreement and suitable English-taught graduate school are available**.

2. **Nanyang Technological University, Singapore — GEM Trailblazer**  
   Best English-medium, professionally oriented Asian option; particularly attractive for communication, computational methods, technology, and regional networking. **Spring 2027 nomination is immediately urgent.**

3. **University of Amsterdam, Netherlands — Global/Faculty Exchange**  
   Strongest likely disciplinary fit for communication science, media, public opinion, and digital society, but housing and living costs are substantial and access depends on a partner agreement.

4. **University of Copenhagen, Denmark — bilateral exchange**  
   Best option for social-science breadth, methodological development, independent academic work, and transparent ECTS credit accounting. High living costs are the principal drawback.

5. **University of Tokyo, Japan — USTEP Type G**  
   Excellent for supervised research, academic networking, and thesis development, but potentially less straightforward for ordinary taught-course credit than Waseda or NTU.

6. **University of Wisconsin–Madison, United States — VISP**  
   The most practical independent-admission fallback: regular university courses and an official transcript without requiring a formal exchange agreement. Its approximately **US$30,639 official graduate-level semester budget** makes it a weak financial fit unless substantial external support is secured.

No option can yet be certified as eligible because the home institution, partner list, degree year, passport, GPA, language scores, budget, and credit policy remain unknown.

---

## 1. Assumptions and confirmation register

### Explicit assumptions

- **Target period:** Spring 2027.
- **Academic level:** Current graduate student who has completed a bachelor’s degree in Journalism and Communication.
- **Preferred workload:** One ordinary full-time semester, normally around **30 ECTS in Europe**, a host-defined full-time course-unit load in Asia, or the relevant graduate full-time load in the United States.
- **Academic objective:** A coherent semester combining new media, public opinion, computational or data methods, society and culture—not a collection of unrelated introductory courses.
- **Budget orientation:** Cost-conscious; tuition-waived exchange is strongly preferred.
- **Visa treatment:** Nationality-neutral. No assumption is made about passport or immigration entitlement.
- **Language:** No English or Japanese test score is assumed.
- **Credit:** No host credit is assumed to transfer automatically.

### Items requiring confirmation before any application

| Required confirmation | Why it is decisive |
|---|---|
| Current university and department | Determines exchange partners, nomination authority, tuition waiver and scholarships |
| Degree level and year | Some programs require a minimum number of completed semesters |
| Spring 2027 registration status | Exchange students normally must remain enrolled at their home university |
| Partner agreements with each host | Waseda, NTU, UvA, Copenhagen and UTokyo generally require institutional nomination |
| Home credit-recognition policy | Determines minimum load, grade conversion, pass/fail acceptance and thesis/residency restrictions |
| Passport nationality | Determines visa category, processing time, financial evidence and travel permissions |
| GPA and transcript | Needed for institutional nomination and host eligibility |
| English score or proof of English-medium study | Requirements differ by institution, school and course |
| Japanese proficiency | Critical if considering Japanese-medium courses |
| Maximum total budget | Necessary to distinguish realistic and unrealistic destinations |
| Spring 2027 exact dates | Japanese spring terms may extend well beyond the end of a typical Chinese spring semester |
| Need for taught credit versus research credit | Particularly important for UTokyo Type G and research-student pathways |
| Supervisor availability | May be mandatory for some Japanese graduate-school placements |
| Whether pass/fail courses transfer | Copenhagen specifically warns that a pass grade cannot later be converted into a numeric grade |
| Course availability and capacity | Exchange admission does not guarantee enrollment in every requested course |

---

# 2. Regional comparison

## United States

### Recommended option: University of Wisconsin–Madison VISP

The Visiting International Student Program is designed for short-term, non-degree international students, including students coming **outside a formal exchange agreement**. Participants are official UW–Madison students, take regular university courses, and receive an official transcript showing courses and grades. The traditional VISP track permits selection across more than 160 departments and programs, subject to availability and prerequisites. [citation:UW–Madison VISP](https://visp.wisc.edu/) [citation:VISP Academics](https://visp.wisc.edu/academics/)

#### Curriculum and teaching model

A possible semester could combine:

- Journalism and Mass Communication;
- communication research;
- sociology or political science;
- statistics, data science or information studies;
- computational methods;
- science and technology studies.

The U.S. model is likely to involve frequent assignments, seminar participation, presentations, office-hour interaction and continuous assessment. This can be valuable for improving academic argumentation and methodological confidence, but it also produces a relatively dense weekly workload.

**Requires confirmation:** whether graduate-level journalism, communication and data courses admit non-degree VISP students, and whether the desired courses are offered in Spring 2027.

#### Credit transfer

The official transcript is a major advantage. For immigration-related full-time enrollment, UW’s published 2026–27 estimate uses a minimum of **eight graduate credits per semester**. That does not mean eight U.S. credits will automatically satisfy a full home semester; the home university must define the conversion. [citation:VISP Cost of Attendance](https://visp.wisc.edu/cost/)

Before applying, obtain written answers to:

1. How many home credits equal one U.S. semester credit?
2. Is eight graduate credits sufficient for home full-time status?
3. Will courses outside the home department count as electives?
4. Is a letter grade required?
5. Are online or pass/fail courses acceptable?

#### Cost and funding

UW’s official 2026–27 graduate-level estimate is:

- Tuition and fees for eight credits: **US$15,659**
- Estimated living expenses used for financial documentation: **US$14,980**
- Total: **US$30,639**
- Additional one-time document fee: **US$130**

The living-expense figure covers six months for immigration-document purposes even though the teaching semester is shorter. UW states that it does not provide individual need- or merit-based scholarships to visiting international students, and visiting international students are not eligible for U.S. federal financial aid. [citation:VISP Cost of Attendance](https://visp.wisc.edu/cost/)

**Assessment:** Academically legitimate and administratively accessible, but poor value for a cost-conscious student unless the home university or an external scholarship covers a large share.

#### Visa and adaptation

If UW issues immigration documentation, the usual category will be determined by the program and applicant’s circumstances, commonly F-1 or J-1. The actual route, interview requirements, financial evidence and processing time must be confirmed after nationality and funding are known.

Practical adaptation issues include:

- high health-insurance and medical costs;
- winter weather in Madison;
- intensive continuous assessment;
- substantial upfront proof-of-funds requirements;
- possible difficulty entering high-demand courses;
- a more direct classroom discussion culture.

#### Research and networking value

UW–Madison offers the strongest U.S. fallback in this shortlist for becoming part of a large research university rather than attending a stand-alone commercial study-abroad program. Its value would rise significantly if the student can identify a faculty member or research group in journalism, communication, political behavior, digital media, misinformation or computational social science before arrival.

### U.S. verdict

- **Academic value:** High
- **Credit documentation:** High
- **Independent access:** High
- **Affordability:** Low
- **Priority:** Backup only

## Europe

## Option A: University of Amsterdam

The UvA Global Exchange Programme is available when the home university has a formal agreement with UvA and formally nominates the student. UvA also operates faculty-level and Erasmus arrangements, so the applicable route may depend on the specific school or department rather than only the university-wide agreement. [citation:UvA Global Exchange Programme](https://www.uva.nl/en/education/exchange/global-exchange-programme/global-exchange-programme.html) [citation:UvA Exchange](https://www.uva.nl/en/education/exchange/exchange.html)

### Curriculum and teaching model

UvA is especially relevant because of its established academic environment in communication and media research. A strong learning agreement would prioritize:

- communication science;
- political communication and public opinion;
- digital media and platform society;
- research methods;
- computational social science;
- sociology, politics or cultural studies.

The likely academic style emphasizes independent reading, critical discussion, research-led instruction and comparatively strict grading. UvA cautions that foreign grade-conversion tables are for broad orientation rather than automatic equivalence. [citation:UvA Academic Climate and Grading](https://www.uva.nl/en/education/exchange/on-exchange-at-the-uva/academic-climate-and-teaching-at-the-uva/academic-climate-and-teaching-at-the-uva.html)

**Requires confirmation:** whether graduate Communication Science courses are available through the relevant agreement; university-wide exchange status does not necessarily grant unrestricted access to every faculty.

### Credit transfer

The ECTS framework makes workload documentation comparatively transparent. A normal European semester is usually constructed around approximately 30 ECTS, but the home university must still approve:

- the ECTS-to-home-credit formula;
- master’s versus bachelor’s course level;
- minimum passing grade;
- pass/fail treatment;
- whether courses across faculties can count;
- whether resit dates extend beyond the permitted visiting period.

### Cost and housing

**Preliminary planning estimate—not an official UvA quotation:** approximately **€1,300–€1,800 per month**, depending heavily on housing. Airfare, visa or residence-permit fees, insurance and deposits are additional.

Amsterdam housing should be treated as a high-risk operational issue. Do not commit to UvA without either university-assisted housing or a verified alternative. Avoid unverified advance payments and ensure registration at the address is permitted.

### Scholarships

UvA advertises a **Global Changemaker Scholarship**, but it is limited to students from a selected group of partner institutions. Eligibility, award amount, nomination procedure and Spring 2027 availability require confirmation. [citation:UvA Global Exchange Programme](https://www.uva.nl/en/education/exchange/global-exchange-programme/global-exchange-programme.html)

### Research and cross-cultural value

UvA is probably the strongest pure disciplinary match in the shortlist. Amsterdam also provides direct exposure to European debates about platform governance, public broadcasting, data protection, migration, urban diversity and digital rights. The main trade-off is that exchange students can easily remain inside an international-student bubble unless they join regular seminars, research events or local organizations.

## Option B: University of Copenhagen

UCPH accepts exchange students for one or two semesters through Erasmus, bilateral, 4EU+, Nordplus or Nordlys agreements. The home university must nominate the student. The published deadline for a spring-semester application is **1 October**, and the spring semester officially runs from **1 February to 30 June**. [citation:UCPH Incoming Exchange](https://studies.ku.dk/study-abroad/exchange/) [citation:UCPH Academic Matters](https://studies.ku.dk/study-abroad/exchange/academic-matters/)

### Curriculum and teaching model

UCPH describes its teaching as a mixture of lectures, tutorials, presentations, projects, practical assignments, laboratory work and fieldwork. Assessments may be papers, written examinations, oral examinations or active participation. [citation:UCPH Academic Matters](https://studies.ku.dk/study-abroad/exchange/academic-matters/)

Relevant areas may include:

- sociology;
- social data science;
- political communication-related electives;
- digital culture and humanities;
- philosophy, culture and European society;
- statistics and social-science methods.

The course catalogue distinguishes bachelor’s and master’s courses and provides an exchange-student filter. The full list normally appears only two to three months before the semester, so prior-year listings should be used only for preliminary planning. UCPH recommends 30 ECTS per semester but permits more or less, subject to course and home-university requirements. [citation:UCPH Course Information](https://studies.ku.dk/study-abroad/exchange/course-information/)

For Social Data Science, the published guidance says that master’s students ordinarily need a bachelor’s degree in political science, economics, psychology, sociology or anthropology, plus course-specific prerequisites. A Journalism and Communication degree may therefore not satisfy the formal background requirement automatically. Sociology normally requires prior social theory, statistics and research-methods coursework. [citation:UCPH Course Information](https://studies.ku.dk/study-abroad/exchange/course-information/)

**Requires confirmation:** whether the journalism/communication transcript meets sociology or social-data prerequisites.

### Credit transfer

UCPH uses ECTS, with 60 ECTS defined as a full academic year. It uses the Danish seven-point grading scale or pass/fail. UCPH explicitly warns that pass grades cannot later be converted into numerical grades, so the home university’s treatment of pass/fail must be checked before registration. [citation:UCPH Academic Matters](https://studies.ku.dk/study-abroad/exchange/academic-matters/)

### Cost and adaptation

**Preliminary planning estimate—not an official UCPH quotation:** approximately **DKK 8,000–12,000 per month**, with housing as the largest variable. Upfront rent and deposits may be substantial.

The academic culture generally rewards preparation, independence, critical discussion and egalitarian interaction. The university offers orientation and mentor/buddy programs, although places are not guaranteed. [citation:UCPH Academic Matters](https://studies.ku.dk/study-abroad/exchange/academic-matters/)

### Language

Many courses are taught in English. Proof is not required for most subjects, but it can be required for specific areas, including Political Science. Danish-taught courses require separate evidence or dispensation. [citation:UCPH Course Information](https://studies.ku.dk/study-abroad/exchange/course-information/)

### Europe verdict

| Criterion | Amsterdam | Copenhagen |
|---|---:|---:|
| Direct communication/media fit | Excellent | Moderate |
| Methods and social-science breadth | Very good | Very good |
| Credit transparency | Very good | Excellent |
| Housing risk | Very high | High |
| Living-cost pressure | High | High |
| Cultural immersion | Excellent | Excellent |
| Best use | Communication/media semester | Broader methods, sociology and culture semester |

## Japan

## Option A: Waseda University exchange

Waseda has published application guidelines and school-specific requirements for **AY2027**, including separate documents for English-based and Japanese-based graduate schools. Applicants must meet all school-specific GPA and language requirements. Some graduate schools require prior approval from a prospective research supervisor. Waseda also warns that course capacity can prevent students from obtaining all desired courses, so it does not guarantee that every student will achieve a home university’s required credit total. [citation:Waseda Exchange Application](https://www.waseda.jp/inst/cie/en/exchange/application)

### Curriculum and teaching model

Waseda is attractive for a student interested in the intersection of:

- media and communication;
- technology and society;
- political and public-opinion research;
- Japanese culture and contemporary society;
- data and information;
- Asia-focused interdisciplinary study.

The correct school must be selected carefully. “English-based program” does not necessarily mean that every desired course is available in English or offered in Spring 2027. The university instructs applicants to use the relevant graduate-school requirement list and course list and notes that offerings are subject to change. [citation:Waseda Exchange Application](https://www.waseda.jp/inst/cie/en/exchange/application)

A Waseda semester is likely to offer more urban, media-industry and cultural exposure than UTokyo, while UTokyo may offer stronger research-lab or supervisor-centered value.

### Credit transfer

The key risk is not institutional legitimacy but **course certainty**. Before nomination, prepare:

- a primary list totaling the required host workload;
- a second list with at least 30–50% more courses;
- home approval for both lists;
- written rules for Japanese credit conversion;
- confirmation that Spring 2027 examinations finish before the home deadline.

Japanese spring terms commonly start later and end later than North American, Singaporean or many Chinese spring semesters. The actual Waseda calendar must therefore be checked against thesis, internship, graduation and next-semester obligations.

### Language

Three routes are possible:

1. English-based graduate-school study;
2. Japanese-based graduate-school study;
3. a mixed plan with Japanese-language study.

The first is the safest without demonstrated Japanese proficiency. Do not assume that conversational Japanese is enough for graduate seminars or written examinations.

### Cost and funding

**Preliminary planning estimate—not an official Waseda quotation:** approximately **JPY 120,000–190,000 per month**, depending on dormitory access and location. Exchange tuition may be waived under the partner agreement, but administrative fees, housing, insurance and local transport require confirmation.

Potential university, home-institution or external scholarships must be checked through the nomination office. Do not build the budget around an unconfirmed award.

### Cross-cultural and networking value

Waseda is likely the best cultural-intellectual match for the profile: it allows engagement with contemporary Japanese media and society while supporting an existing interest in Japanese literature and culturally rich nonfiction. Tokyo also offers access to universities, media organizations, technology firms, museums, archives and public events.

The main adaptation challenges are:

- administrative procedures;
- indirect communication conventions;
- smaller English-language course pool than expected;
- possible separation between exchange and local students;
- competitive housing;
- calendar misalignment.

## Option B: University of Tokyo USTEP Type G

UTokyo’s university-wide exchange program accepts students only from partner universities, with applications submitted through the partner university’s exchange office. Type G is the graduate route. Students may have the status of **Special Auditor** or **Special Research Student**, and graduate-school requirements differ. [citation:UTokyo USTEP](https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/academics/ustep.html) [citation:UTokyo USTEP Type G](https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/academics/ustep-type-g.html)

### Best use case

UTokyo Type G should be prioritized when the objective is:

- supervised research;
- thesis or dissertation development;
- connection with a specific professor or laboratory;
- methods development;
- long-term PhD preparation.

It is less obviously optimal when the home university demands a conventional semester composed mainly of examinable, graded taught courses. A Special Research Student placement may produce research documentation rather than a normal package of course credits.

### Admissions and visa support

Applicants must first be nominated by the home university. For successful applicants, UTokyo provides a Certificate of Admission and assists with the Certificate of Eligibility process used for immigration preparation. UTokyo’s page states that Spring Admission results are normally announced in early December. [citation:UTokyo USTEP Type G](https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/academics/ustep-type-g.html)

**Requires confirmation:**

- partner status;
- Type G Spring 2027 nomination deadline;
- graduate-school-specific language and GPA requirements;
- need for a supervisor;
- Special Auditor versus Special Research Student status;
- transcript and credit issuance;
- whether the research activity counts toward the home degree.

### Cost and cultural value

Use the same preliminary Tokyo planning range as Waseda—**JPY 120,000–190,000 per month**—until a host budget and housing offer are available.

UTokyo offers exceptional research prestige and network value, but the semester should be organized around a named professor, research unit or methodological objective. Without that anchor, Waseda or NTU is likely to provide a more coherent taught-credit experience.

### Japan verdict

| Criterion | Waseda | UTokyo Type G |
|---|---:|---:|
| Taught-course flexibility | Better | Depends on graduate school/status |
| Media/cultural fit | Excellent | Good |
| Research-supervision value | Very good | Excellent |
| Ordinary-credit simplicity | Moderate | Potentially difficult |
| Need for advance faculty contact | Sometimes | Often strategically important |
| Recommended priority | First Japan choice | Research-oriented alternative |

## Singapore

## Recommended option: NTU GEM Trailblazer

NTU’s GEM Trailblazer program permits international students to study or conduct research for one or two semesters while earning credit toward their home degree. It is open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from partner universities, and formal home-university nomination is mandatory. [citation:NTU GEM Trailblazer](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/education/student-exchanges/inbound-programmes)

### Eligibility and immediate deadline

NTU publishes the following general conditions:

- active formal agreement with the home university;
- nomination by the home university;
- full-time enrollment at home;
- at least two completed semesters, with separate conditions for direct-master’s applicants seeking postgraduate courses;
- minimum CGPA of 3.3/5 or equivalent;
- English proficiency.

For Semester 2, running approximately January–May, NTU’s published cycle lists:

- nomination: **1–15 September**;
- application: **1–30 September**.

Because the research date is **15 September 2026**, the nomination inquiry is immediately urgent. The dates are stated to be subject to change, so the home exchange office and NTU must confirm whether a Spring 2027 nomination can still be submitted. [citation:NTU GEM Trailblazer](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/education/student-exchanges/inbound-programmes)

### Curriculum and teaching model

A strong NTU plan would investigate courses in:

- communication and information;
- public opinion and media effects;
- digital journalism;
- social-media analytics;
- computational communication;
- data science or AI;
- technology policy;
- Asian societies and cultures.

NTU asks applicants to indicate at least ten courses; the home university should approve them as relevant to academic progression. This is helpful for contingency planning but also signals that first-choice enrollment is not guaranteed. [citation:NTU GEM Trailblazer](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/education/student-exchanges/inbound-programmes)

NTU is likely to offer a structured, assessment-intensive model, commonly involving lectures, tutorials, projects, presentations and examinations. It is particularly suitable for students comfortable with quantitative work and Python.

### Credit transfer

Before application:

1. Obtain the host course-unit value and contact-hour information.
2. Map each NTU course to a home elective or requirement.
3. Secure approval for at least ten candidate courses.
4. Confirm the minimum full-time load.
5. Confirm whether postgraduate course access is permitted.
6. Obtain approval for backup undergraduate courses if graduate enrollment fails.
7. Confirm transcript timing and grade conversion.

### Costs and scholarships

**Preliminary planning estimate—not an official NTU quotation:** approximately **SGD 1,400–2,300 per month**, with housing availability as the largest uncertainty.

NTU states that it does **not** offer scholarships or financial assistance to ordinary exchange students and that participants should be prepared to cover their full costs. The DUO-Singapore award described by NTU is invitation-only, applies to certain paired European–Singapore exchanges, and is tied to Semester 1 rather than a normal Spring/Semester 2 placement. It should therefore not be assumed available here. [citation:NTU GEM Trailblazer](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/education/student-exchanges/inbound-programmes)

### Visa and adaptation

Accepted students receive guidance concerning the Student’s Pass, housing and course registration. The exact entry and pass requirements depend on nationality and should be checked only after admission. [citation:NTU GEM Trailblazer](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/education/student-exchanges/inbound-programmes)

Singapore offers the easiest linguistic adaptation in the Asian shortlist because English is the academic working language. It also provides a highly relevant comparative setting for studying:

- technology governance;
- multicultural communication;
- state–society relations;
- platform use and public opinion;
- Southeast Asian media;
- urban digital infrastructure.

Practical concerns include heat and humidity, high private-housing costs, intensive coursework and the need to move quickly when university accommodation is released.

## Why Waseda is first

Waseda provides the best balance of subject relevance, cultural immersion, Asian intellectual context and probable affordability under exchange. It falls below first place if:

- there is no partner agreement;
- only Japanese-medium graduate study is available;
- Spring 2027 courses cannot form an approved full load;
- its calendar conflicts with home obligations.

## Why NTU could become first

NTU should move to first place if the student wants:

- an English-medium environment;
- computational or technology-oriented communication;
- January–May calendar compatibility;
- relatively easy daily adaptation;
- Southeast Asian rather than primarily Japanese cultural exposure.

## Why UvA could become first

UvA should move to first place if the home institution has a relevant faculty agreement and the student can obtain housing. It is likely the strongest direct match for communication science and public-opinion research.

# 4. Recommended academic designs

A semester should be approved as a **coherent academic package**, not merely a destination experience.

## Plan A: Computational communication

- Public opinion or political communication
- Social-media/platform research
- Quantitative or computational methods
- Data ethics or technology governance
- Host-country society/culture course

Best fits: **NTU, UvA, UCPH**

## Plan B: Media, society and culture

- Digital media theory
- Journalism or media institutions
- Sociology of culture
- Host-country society/politics
- Language or intercultural course

Best fits: **Waseda, UvA, UCPH**

## Plan C: Thesis-development semester

- Supervised research project
- Advanced methods seminar
- Relevant substantive seminar
- Research workshop or colloquium
- Deliverable linked to home thesis

Best fits: **UTokyo Type G, Waseda, UvA**

The thesis-development route must be approved especially carefully. A host supervisor’s letter is not necessarily equivalent to graded course credit.
